title: Standardized Protocol for Human Milk Collection and Storage in a Multicenter Study
author: Isabella Costa

steps.title: Screen Participants for Eligibility
steps.instruction: Verify that the participant meets all inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria.

substeps.instruction: Confirm inclusion: Lactating women aged ≥18 years, ≥7 days postpartum, gestational age ≥34 weeks at delivery, no contraindications to breastfeeding, and no signs of breast infection or nipple injury.
Confirm exclusion: Ensure no cold chain disruption (thawing or storage outside refrigeration for >30 minutes) and no visible contamination of milk with blood or purulent secretion.
Verify milk production is established (≥7 days postpartum).
Confirm the last breastfeeding session occurred at least 1 hour prior to collection.

steps.title: Obtain Informed Consent
steps.instruction: Explain study objectives and procedures to the participant and obtain written consent.

substeps.instruction: Present the Informed Consent Form (ICF) and allow time for reading and questions.
Obtain written informed consent in duplicate.
Provide one signed copy to the participant and store the second copy securely.

steps.title: Prepare Materials and Labeling
steps.instruction: Set up the collection station and prepare identification codes for sample traceability.

substeps.instruction: Prepare three 5 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock tubes, one 3 mL disposable Pasteur pipette, and one sterile 50 mL collection container on a clean, stable surface.
Assign a unique alphanumeric identification code to the participant based on recruitment site and enrollment order.
Label the three Eppendorf tubes with the identical identification code using a waterproof permanent marker.

steps.title: Prepare Participant and Researcher
steps.instruction: Ensure the environment and personnel are ready for hygienic sample collection.

substeps.instruction: Seat the participant comfortably, preferably without holding the infant.
Researcher must perform hand hygiene and don a surgical mask, disposable gown, and disposable gloves.
Inspect both breasts for signs of infection or nipple injury; if identified, discontinue the procedure.

steps.title: Collect Human Milk
steps.instruction: Collect breast milk via manual self-expression into a sterile container.

substeps.instruction: Instruct the participant to wash her hands thoroughly.
Provide the sterile 50 mL collection container without the lid.
Instruct the participant to perform manual self-expression from behind the nipple directly into the container.
Request approximately 10 mL of milk, alternating between breasts if necessary to obtain the volume.

steps.title: Aliquot Milk Samples
steps.instruction: Divide the collected milk into the prepared tubes.

substeps.instruction: Place the collected milk on a stable surface.
Using a disposable Pasteur pipette, aliquot the milk equally across the three labeled Eppendorf tubes (e.g., if 6 mL total, aliquot 2 mL per tube).

steps.title: Store Samples
steps.instruction: Secure the aliquots in a labeled storage box and freeze.

substeps.instruction: Place labeled tubes into a cardboard storage box suitable for microtubes.
Label the box with the study name, responsible researcher, and a 'Do Not Handle' notice.
Store the box in a freezer at −12°C to −18°C.

steps.title: Collect and Link Data
steps.instruction: Record maternal, newborn, and environmental data using the standardized digital platform.

substeps.instruction: Collect maternal data: age, education, prenatal history, diabetes/hypertension/anemia status, delivery mode, gestational age, anthropometric data, and erythrogram results.
Collect neonatal data: birth weight and multiple pregnancy status.
Collect breastfeeding data: time since last session, breastfeeding type, and collection observations.
Collect environmental data: ambient temperature, relative humidity, and geographic location (for THI calculation).
Link all data to the participant-specific identification code to ensure traceability between biological samples and records.
